fact: A hot super-Earth at Lalande 21185 — one of the nearest planet-hosting stars.
bio: GJ 411 b is a super-Earth whipping around Lalande 21185, a dim red dwarf about eight light-years away in the Great Bear and one of the closest stars to the Sun. First detected in 2017 and confirmed in 2020 from the star's tiny velocity wobble, it orbits far too close to be habitable, but its nearness makes the system a recurring waypoint in interstellar-travel fiction.
